spokenTurns.cue: [NB_ITEM] Say exactly: "Three is the whole. One part is one. What is the other part?" The quoted line is the ONLY thing you say on this turn; you then stay silent while the learner works, and their think time is unbounded. Never say the answer during their turn and never count aloud with them. The correct answer is "two". The question already says "three" and "one" out loud, so those numbers said back are NOT the answer, however confident it sounds. Counting up aloud is the learner working, not answering — judge the number they OFFER when the counting stops. "two", "two more", or "two" said after counting up all count as two. If the answer is right, say exactly: "Yes, two — two and one make three." and stop there — add no praise, no encouragement and no mention of what comes next. If it is wrong, say exactly: "My turn: start at one and count up to three: two, three. That is two more. Your turn. One part is one — what is the other part?" and stop there; that correction is the whole turn, and it is the SAME line on every wrong answer, including a repeat of the same wrong answer — never paraphrase it, never soften it, and never replace it with a hint of your own.
